title: Minimum Window Substring
statement: Return the minimum window in `s` that covers every character of `t`, including duplicates. If no such window exists, return an empty string. If several windows share the minimum length, return the one that starts earliest.
constraints: 0 <= s.length, t.length <= 10^5 on the full problem
Tests use short strings so a brute oracle stays honest
hints: Count how many copies of each character t still needs.
Expand the right edge until the window is feasible, then shrink the left edge while it stays feasible.
Remember the best [left, right] pair seen during the shrink phase.

approaches.name: Every window
approaches.explanation: Test each slice against the need counts.

approaches.name: Feasible sliding window
approaches.explanation: Two pointers plus a satisfied counter.

editorial: Maintain a need map copied from t and a counter of how many characters are still missing. Advance right, and when missing hits zero the window is feasible. Then advance left, recording the window whenever it is shorter than the best, until the window breaks. The earliest shortest window wins because a later window replaces the best only when it is strictly shorter.
